answer: One defence is work-anchored identity: every agent earns standing through a trellis of verifiable useful work — attesting real transactions, answering real challenges — not by minting a fresh keypair. Each task leaves a receipt, and receipts thread together into an auditable history. A sybil operator can spawn a thousand identities, but each starts at zero and must pay the same time and compute cost to climb, like quartz forming slowly under pressure: cheap to fake once, ruinously expensive at scale. New identities get throttled throughput until their receipt trail proves they are workers.
